note: Window agent m0300-m0201, 2 Nov 2026. Two inverted vassal relations cancelled and redrawn the right way round (Rome/Greek cities, Mauretania/Numidia), one vassal drawn as independent (Hán), three keyframes widened where the dossier's own events or text say more (Rome 216, Han 204, Qin 222), and the zombie Han and Wei shapes inside Qin removed. Every entry rests on a page opened in that run. Reviewer (m0300-m0201 review, 2 Nov 2026): keyframe_overrides/3 to /6 added to complete events/0, events/1 (Rome no longer a vassal exposed Baetica 206-204 and Etruria 225-224 to too-narrow keyframes) and events/5, events/6 (the former Han and Daliang were left to nobody or Chu in 230-224); keyframe_overrides/1 why corrected (Liu Ying, not Xiao He, was put in charge of Yueyang); keyframe_overrides/0 and /4 leave out the Ligurian north-west of Tuscany (the ligures dossier holds it). Seam agent sm-03 (3 Nov 2026): keyframe_overrides/7 to /12 added, giving Sogdia and Bactria to the Seleucid shapes of 291, 283, 281, 279, 277 and 264 (seam item from m0400-m0301). Orchestrator 3 Nov 2026: dropped events [0, 1] (fx-49: greek-city-states ledger 58/72 deleted; these closed Rome's Magna Graecia relation in its start year).

events.note: Cancels mauretania/ledger/1 as the compiler reads it. The dossier's own note is right ('King Bokkar of Morocco becomes Masinissa's vassal'), but a vassal_start in mauretania with counterpart kingdom-of-numidia means Numidia becomes Mauretania's vassal, so Numidia was drawn in Mauretania's tint from 202 (1,100 cell-years, to the end of the window and beyond). The page: 'Following the capture of Syphax, the King Bokkar, ruler of what is now Morocco with his capital based in Tingis, had become a vassal of Masinissa.'

Returns Mauretania's own land (its Cliopatria shape of 212-197, about 190 cells) that closing the wrong relation hands back to nobody because Numidia is not yet alive in 203; the land is Mauretania's in the dossier's keyframes and in the draft before this patch.

The relation the right way round: Mauretania the vassal of Masinissa's Numidia. The page: 'Following the capture of Syphax [Cirta, 203 BC], the King Bokkar, ruler of what is now Morocco ... had become a vassal of Masinissa'; a French source cited there has 'En 202 avant Jésus-Christ, après la capture de Syphax, il devint le vassal de Massinissa'. 202 is Numidia's first year; mauretania/ledger/3 (148) ends it.

correction.text: the dossier's own correction (the shape without Hannibal's Italian allies in the south and without southern Spain), plus Tuscany, Umbria and the Marche: Cliopatria's 216-213 shape holds only 65 of their 153 cells, which leaves a hole in central Italy in the year of Cannae although Hannibal's march through Etruria, Umbria and to the Adriatic coast took no land, Arretium was a Roman supply base and 'the majority of Rome's allies in central Italy remained loyal'

keyframe_overrides.why: Second Punic War page: after Trasimene 'The Carthaginians continued their march through Etruria, then Umbria, to the Adriatic coast', Arretium is a Roman base ('established supply depots at Ariminum and Arretium'), and 'the majority of Rome's allies in central Italy remained loyal' after Cannae; only Capua, Tarentum, two Samnite tribes and the south went over. This override restates the dossier's correction for the shape and adds the three central-Italian regions so that Rome's land there is not trimmed to nobody once the Greek-city-states tint (events/0, events/1) stops hiding the shortfall. [Reviewer: Tuscany now leaves out the Ligurian north-west (Apuan Alps, Garfagnana, Lunigiana); with the whole of Toscana the override took the 6 cells the ligures dossier holds there in 216 and left them to nobody from 212.]

keyframe_overrides.why: Chu-Han Contention page: Liu Bang moved east of Hangu Pass 'after conquering the Three Qins in the Guanzhong region' (205), 'Sima Xin, the King of Sai, Dong Yi, the King of Di, and Shen Yang, the King of Henan, surrendered to Liu Bang' (205), he 'attacked Henei' in April-May 205, and in July-August 205 he named his son Liu Ying heir and 'put him in charge of Yueyang (... present-day Yanliang District, Xi’an)' [reviewer: the window agent's text had Xiao He here; the page names Liu Ying]; the page has no sentence in which Han loses Guanzhong in 204. The dossier's 204 keyframe (Cliopatria's Han of 206, whose bbox ends at 34.4 N, with Wei and Dai) drops the 627 Shaanxi cells and the Yin cells the 205 keyframe holds, so the Han kingdom's own heartland goes to nobody for 204 and returns at the 203 shape.

keyframe_overrides.why: Seam item from m0400-m0301: its keyframe_overrides/13 keeps Sogdia and Bactria in the Seleucid realm for 301-292, but the next keyframe, seleucid-empire_-291 (ok, the Cliopatria outline, years 291-284), lacks them (about 560 Sogdian and 300 Bactrian cells of the gazetteer regions; the published draft's snap at 291 strips 797 cells there: Navoi 363, Gorno-Badakhshan 166, Bukhoro 81) and hands them to nobody. Seleucid Empire page: 'Towards the end of Antiochus II's reign, various provinces simultaneously asserted their independence, such as Bactria and Sogdiana under Diodotus' and 'Diodotus, the Seleucid governor for the Bactrian territory, asserted independence in around 245 BC'; the page names only Gedrosia, Arachosia and the land west of the Indus as ceded to Chandragupta, so Sogdia and Bactria stay Seleucid until the secession. The union leaves out the 67 cells of the Badakhshan mountains (35.6-37.5 N, 70.7-75.0 E) that Cliopatria's Maurya shape of 291-257 holds and that Maurya keeps at 292 under the m0400 entry, so that the Seleucid snap does not take them from Maurya at 291. Entries 8 to 12 below give the same union to the later shapes 283, 281, 279, 277 and 264, each of which lacks the same land and would strip it again at its own start. The 256 shape is left as drawn: from 256 the Greco-Bactrian dossier founds its state in Bactria, and the Sogdian fringe that none of that state's shapes holds then goes to nobody (the page has Bactria and Sogdiana asserting independence together).

rulings.why: Hán Xin 'was made King of Hán (韓王) in 205 BC by Liu Bang' and held 'the lands around Yingchuan as his vassal kingdom, with the capital at Yangzhai'; he is called a vassal of the Han from 202. The dossiers keep the land (han-2 wins the size rule on about 400 cells a year against Cliopatria's Han shapes of 205-203) but draw it as an independent state in the same red as Han; this makes it the Han kingdom's vassal for the years the two shapes overlap.

'King Jia of Wei surrendered and Wei came under Qin control' (225), 'The Qin government established the commanderies of Dang and Sishui in the former Wei territories'; summary table '225 BC: Wei was conquered by Qin.' The Wei dossier says Wei has no land in 224-209 (wei_-223 'empty'), but the size rule keeps the 58-cell Daliang shape for the smaller Wei against Qin's keyframes of 225-222; this gives the 33 cells that remain after qin events/6 to Qin.
